You are one role in an autonomous ML research agent for KuaiRand-Pure.
The immutable task is within-user ranking of long_view using validation GAUC and nDCG@5.
Use train and validation only. Never request or infer hidden-test information. Do not change
the official evaluator, split, label, budgets, or reference files. Return only the requested
structured output. Evidence must be attributable to a supplied method card or primary source.
Every role response is parsed as JSON; never return Markdown, commentary, or text outside the
single requested JSON object.

EDA roles produce compact planning/report artifacts only. They do not generate candidate.py,
modify raw data, change evaluators, or inspect hidden-test data. Prefer train-only evidence
and leakage-safe feature hypotheses compatible with registered families: bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task.

## Data Quality

- 239 videos with zero duration (24,076 train rows affected)
- 15,609 exact duplicate rows in the training-period log
- Sentinel: is_live_streamer = -124 on 21,127 of 27,285 user rows
- UNKNOWN values: user_active_degree (6), video_type (1), upload_type (80)
- Constant columns: is_lowactive_period, visible_status, is_rand
- hourmin encodes hour times 100 in UTC+8
- The training-period log begins on 20220409, not 20220408

## Feature Coverage

- Video features: 100.000 % of train+valid video IDs found in the feature table
- User features: 100.000 % of train+valid user IDs found in the profile table

## Leakage Flag

The video statistics table is a period aggregate over full-platform traffic.
Implied total shows: 12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged
exposures (ratio approximately 4,892 to one). Observation periods per video
range 45 to 181, exceeding the interaction log span.
Legal for use, but any feature derived from it must be caveated as leaky.

## Metric Conventions

- Task: within-user ranking (each user's impressions ranked against each other)
- nDCG@5: sorts by score with a stable sort (ties fall back to row order)
- AUC: averages ranks over ties (Mann-Whitney U)
- GAUC: per-user AUC, only users with 0 < positives < impressions,
  weighted by positive count
- Zero-positive users: nDCG recorded as 0.0 and included in the average
- Primary score = mean(GAUC, nDCG@5)

## Measured Dead Ends

- Adding all 13 static feature fields: primary 0.5940 vs 0.5950 for the default 5
- Embedding dimension k = 8 / 16 / 32: primary 0.5895 / 0.5902 / 0.5887 (flat)
- The bottleneck is not features or capacity
- First-order user-only terms contribute exactly 0 to within-user ranking
  (any term constant within a user does not change intra-group ordering)


ROLE: EDA Builder
Produce a compact UI-visible EDA and feature-engineering report from this plan.
You may infer only from the supplied DATA CARD and experiment history; do not invent exact statistics that are not present.
Separate observations from implications. Every feature candidate must state implementation scope and leakage risk.
Favor feature candidates compatible with src.models.features, history_features, multi_task, BPR, or group_softmax.
Return concise JSON: at most 3 findings, 3 feature candidates, and 3 UI notes. One sentence per field.

feature_candidates.description: Weight user historical long_view by a per-tab half-life based on event recency (hourmin) so recent interactions matter more within each tab.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Capture differential engagement decay across tabs, improving nDCG@5 given tab4's much higher long_view.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Extend history_features to compute per-tab decayed prior using training-time hourmin differences.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; derived strictly from training history timestamps, no future data.
feature_candidates.name: Tab-stratified recency decay weights

feature_candidates.description: Add log(video_age_in_days+1) as a feature conditioned on tab to model novelty effects on long_view propensity.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Distinguish old vs new videos differently per tab; tab4 may prefer newer content, improving ranking.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute video age from video table (non-leaky) relative to train timestamps; concatenate with tab embedding.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if age uses train-period reference epoch; must avoid validation/test future dates.
feature_candidates.name: Video age × tab interaction

feature_candidates.description: User's historical long_view rate per author within each tab, smoothed, to strengthen preference signals.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Better exploit author affinity inside a tab, especially where author–tab patterns are stable.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add (user_author, tab) aggregation to history_features pipeline.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; uses user interaction history only, must exclude current-row interaction during train.
feature_candidates.name: Author-tab cross aggregate for user history

findings.implication: Incorporating tab interaction into history_features (e.g., per-tab historical rates and decay) should improve within-user ranking.
findings.observation: Tab4 has 48.93% long_view rate vs 38.61% for tab1 and 4.22% for tab0, with 73% of rows in tab1.
findings.title: Tab-specific long_view propensity is highly differential

findings.implication: Further refinement of history_features (video age, author-tab) is more promising than loss-function tuning.
findings.observation: hist_prior_days_var_gs2_3b9a achieves primary 0.6045 (GAUC 0.6707, nDCG 0.5382), while BPR and group_softmax only reach ~0.55.
findings.title: history_features with tab×recency dominates classic losses

findings.implication: Derived per-video long_view propensity must remain diagnostic; time-safe recency and user history features should be used instead.
findings.observation: Implied exposures ~12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged (≈4892:1); observation periods exceed log span.
findings.title: Video statistics table is leaky and unusable for training

data.recommended_next_focus: Refine history_features with per-tab recency decay and video-age interaction, while keeping video statistics out of training due to leakage.
data.summary: Within-user long_view ranking is best served by history_features with tab-specific recency and author cross-aggregates; tab4 shows far higher long_view (48.93%) than tab1 (38.61%) and tab0 (4.22%). Video statistics are period aggregates over full platform traffic and are leaky; use only for diagnostics.
ui_notes: Tab4 long_view rate 48.93% vs tab1 38.61% — consider tab-aware priors.
